searchText: I have found this page at some point but cannot seem to find it again. Is there a page somewhere which explicitly defines what `P` and `B_32` is? (e.g. in https://github.com/ethereum/devp2p/blob/master/caps/snap.md#getaccountrange-0x00 -> `[reqID: P, rootHash: B_32, startingHash: B_32, limitHash: B_32, responseBytes: P]`) also a related question to this, if rootHash for e.g. has leading `00` bytes, like 0x000001222..., then can it be send like '0x01222'...? if its a full 32 bytes long, wouldn't it be better to strip off those zeros and save data bandwidth? I'm sure there is, but I don't have a link. However, a B_32 is fixed-size 32 byte, so a hash. Whereas P is arbitrary size byte array Why would a roothash ever have any significant number of leading zeros? One network optimization to be aware ofz though, is > accBody: Account body in slim format I.e: not in trie consensus format thanks! yes (<@508125616940515329>) realized that yea roothash is a bad example, account hashes (for e.g. in AccountRange/GetStorageRanges etc could have leading 00ss for syncing on range) but yes mostly unlikely there as well, as highly probable hash of something not having leading zeros so the real data would most likely not have it i guess Also, let's not forget that the whole thing is snappy compressed too, so inefficiencies like repeated patterns are somewhat made moot by that ohh yes, that would compress it away! thanks <@211091239112671234> 🙏 for this Syncing a OVH-cloud dedicated machine now, from scratch. ** Account/slot + blocks ** ``` Sep 05 16:36:54 orangina geth INFO [09-05|14:36:54.938] State sync in progress synced=0.46% state=928.60MiB accounts=987,692@197.46MiB slots=3,460,491@700.24MiB codes=9783@30.90MiB eta=-384.452ms ... Sep 05 18:49:50 orangina geth INFO [09-05|16:49:50.639] State sync in progress synced=43.51% state=84.41GiB accounts=80,070,378@18.18GiB slots=320,709,853@64.37GiB codes=320,861@1.85GiB eta=2h52m35.845s Sep 05 18:50:06 orangina geth INFO [09-05|16:50:06.364] Imported new block receipts count=104 elapsed=249.467ms number=10,008,538 hash=4c2276..3d295e age=2y4mo1w size=2.10MiB ... Sep 05 21:54:56 orangina geth INFO [09-05|19:54:56.489] State sync in progress synced=79.83% state=155.63GiB accounts=147,158,882@33.36GiB slots=595,514,278@119.02GiB codes=542,235@3.24GiB eta=1h19m40.984s ... Sep 06 00:47:10 orangina geth INFO [09-05|22:47:10.797] State sync in progress synced=100.00% state=198.65GiB accounts=184,202,366@41.79GiB slots=765,616,475@152.87GiB codes=658,358@3.99GiB eta=-3m14.052s ``` So it started at `16:34`and at `18:50` it had downloaded 10M blocks(+bodies), `84GiB` state, at an estimated `43%`. It's own estimate is that it will finish that phase roughly five hours after it started. It completed the account/slot parts at `00:47`, so in roughly `8h:13m`.

excerpts.content:
One network optimization to be aware ofz though, is 

> accBody: Account body in slim format

excerpts.author: holiman
excerpts.content: I.e: not in trie consensus format

excerpts.author: g11tech
excerpts.content: yea roothash is a bad example, account hashes (for e.g. in AccountRange/GetStorageRanges etc could have leading 00ss for syncing on range)

excerpts.author: g11tech
excerpts.content: but yes mostly unlikely there as well, as highly probable hash of something not having leading zeros

excerpts.author: g11tech
excerpts.content: so the real data would most likely not have it i guess

excerpts.author: holiman
excerpts.content: Also, let's not forget that the whole thing is snappy compressed too, so inefficiencies like repeated patterns are somewhat made moot by that
